design_evaluation.summary: A polished dark/light personal tech hub with a clear hero (headline, stats, CTAs), consistent navigation across breakpoints, working theme toggle, visible keyboard focus ring, and a well-structured login modal. Main deductions: the floating Voice Agent button overlaps card content on desktop and mobile, the mobile menu overlay is semi-transparent allowing background content to bleed through, and secondary text in light-theme cards has weak contrast.
strengths: Strong hero hierarchy: large two-line headline, supporting paragraph, stats strip, and distinct primary (Live Feed) vs secondary (AI Lab) CTAs (ui-home-desktop).
Theme toggle works cleanly: layout, nav, and component styling remain consistent between dark and light modes with only intentional accent changes (ui-theme-toggle).
Keyboard focus is clearly indicated with a visible outline on the 'Explore' nav item (ui-keyboard-focus).
Login modal is well organized: Login/Register tabs with active underline, labeled Email/Password fields, gradient submit button, 'Forgot password?' link, and a close X (ui-login-modal).
Mobile menu provides all six nav destinations with adequate tap-target spacing and a full-width 'Break it' action (ui-mobile-menu).
Consistent card pattern across the four tool cards: icon, title, description, and a distinct colored action link (Explore/Scan/Verify/Check).
issues: The fixed 'Voice Agent' button overlaps the 'Reliability & Fact Check' card, partially obscuring its description text and the 'Check →' link on desktop (ui-home-desktop) and again over card content on mobile (ui-mobile-menu).
The mobile menu overlay is semi-transparent; hero stats ('7 RSS SOURCES', '24/7') and CTAs visibly bleed through behind the menu items, reducing readability (ui-mobile-menu).
In light theme, card description text (e.g., 'Stress-test your AI...') and 'Check →' link sit on a light muted background with low contrast (ui-theme-toggle).
The modal close 'X' is small and low-contrast against the dark backdrop; a larger hit area or explicit 'Close' affordance would improve usability (ui-login-modal).
The vertical 'LIVE' badge overlaps the left edge and its red indicator dot extends oddly over the nav bar area, slightly distracting from the hero content (ui-home-desktop).

candidate_findings.title: article-proxy-ssrf-guard
candidate_findings.expected: The proxy must refuse private-network/loopback destinations with a client-error status and a controlled JSON or plain error body; no internal content, stack trace, or 5xx should be returned.
candidate_findings.actual: The SSRF guard itself functions correctly: the endpoint refused to fetch the loopback URL and returned a controlled JSON body ({"error": "refused fetch: private/internal IP 127.0.0.1", "image": null, "title": null}) with no internal content, stack trace, sensitive markers, or 5xx. However, the stated positive expectation required a client-error status (400/403/422) and the endpoint returned HTTP 200 with the error embedded in the body. Since the semantic expectation explicitly includes a 4xx status as part of the controlled-rejection contract, the observation does not fully match the expectation, even though the security-relevant behavior (no fetch of the private resource) is satisfied.
reproduction_steps: Compare the sanitized response with the declared semantic contract.
